question.problem: The price $P,$ in dollars, of electricity in a certain city is directly proportional to the consumption $C,$ measured in kilowatt-hour ($\text{kWh}).$ When the consumption is $C=24\,\text{kWh},$ the price is $P=$264.$ What is the constant of variation?
question.worked_solution:
The price $P$ is directly proportional to the consumption $C,$ so we have

$$
P=kC,
$$

where $k$ is the constant of variation.

We are told that when the consumption is $C=24\,\text{kWh},$ the price is $P=$264.$ We can use this information to solve for $k,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}264 & =k\cdot (24) \\ 264 & =24k \\ \frac{264}{24} & =k \\ 11 & =k\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since $k=\frac{P}{C},$ we have that the units of $k$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{dollars}}{\text{kWh}} & =\text{dollars per kilowatt-hour}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our final answer is $k=$11$ per kilowatt-hour.
